analysis:
The only change in this PR is in the test file provider-swift/Tests/ClusterPlacementChecks/PlacementSetupCheck.swift, at head lines 1260-1264. The existing `publicTrafficLine` assertion now passes `publicModels: []`, so the 'not yet qualified' expectation is tested with records only and no public declaration. The base text (1263-1422) and head text (1-333) show no production code, authentication, key handling, attestation, cache storage or coordinator interaction in the changed lines. The surrounding tests exercise the cluster placement and serving-grant logic, the hand-off opt-in, the developer-only bench cap, bench chip and forced-mode settings (which release builds refuse), and the record-based public grants. They assert the intended fail-closed behavior.

The test edit implies a changed signature for `ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine`, probably an added `publicModels` parameter. A new public-declaration mechanism for public-traffic qualification may therefore exist in non-test source that was not supplied here. If so, how it authorizes public serving and whether it can bypass the qualification-record requirement should be examined in the source files that implement it. This test change gives no evidence of a regression. The threat model does not appear to cover cluster placement or public-grant policy directly, so the next pass should check the parameter's default and its production callers. No threat IDs are implicated by the changed lines.
